Overview runs all six lanes at once. Each person's own tab replays their beats one at a time.
Each cell carries an evidence chip: live (a request just made), rbac (role assignment read live), logs
(read back from Log Analytics) or design (not run). A person who has not signed in once (key P)
The budget mails the resource-group Owners at 50, 80
and 100 % of actual spend and at 100 % forecast. Azure
bills hours late. No price per token is shown.
Alternate: abw-agent-rpm set to 1 gives HTTP 429
rate_limited with Retry-After of about 100 s. Both are global
settings: use a demo tenant only.
Different person, different answer, read from the token. The agent enters through the same gateway, and spend and a per-user token ceiling are visible and enforced.
- Each act reads left to right: what is tried, the control that decides, and the result. Red results are refusals (or the legacy leak); the chips under each panel name the walls it exercises.
- Different acts stop the request at different walls: the gateway (W1), the MCP server (W2), the data plane (W3) and the guardrail (W0). Act 2 proves keys are off, and Act 5 shows how
- Act 7 runs as real people: a different answer per persona, the agent's front door, the bill and a live token budget. A persona that has not signed in once shows design, a predicted
APIM gateway: token, role, client, rate, kill switch
Data plane: its own roles, on the user's own token
Azure Policy: rules on the Azure resources
Result colour: red = refused or leaked, white = allowed
